How to Run a Corporate Charity Bike Build: A Planner’s Guide

By James Carter, founder of Legendary Team Building · Updated November 2026
Planning Guide6 min readBy James Carter, founder of Legendary Team BuildingUpdated November 2026
Quick answer

A corporate charity bike build is a team building event in which employees assemble real bikes that are donated to children. Legendary Team Building runs it as Building a Dream: teams of five earn parts, build a road-ready bike, and then the children arrive to receive it. It typically runs about two hours (60 to 180 minutes), works for groups of 5 to 5,000, and costs $100 to $175 per person with the donated bikes included. Plan around four decisions: headcount, room, recipient and length.

What a corporate charity bike build is

The format is simple. Employees split into teams, compete in short challenges to earn bike components, and then assemble a complete bike from the frame up. The bikes are donated to children in the host community. What separates a well-run build from a service project is the handoff: the children come to the event, and the team sees who the work is for.

Legendary Team Building has run this format since 2003 and has donated more than 50,000 bikes. In 2017 it produced the Guinness World Record–setting charity bike build for DaVita, with 5,000 employees building bikes for 1,000 children.

Run of show

A typical two-hour build moves through four phases. A shorter session compresses the middle; a longer one adds more framing and debrief.

  1. Frame the day. Participants start in theater seating for a short, customizable opener that connects the build to your message, such as a kickoff theme, a values refresh or a merger.
  2. Earn the parts. Teams of five compete in quick challenges to earn the components of their bike.
  3. Build. Teams move to build tables and assemble a complete bike from a clear kit. The event crew safety-checks every finished bike.
  4. The reveal and wrap-up. The children arrive, the team forms a human tunnel, and the kids ride in on the bikes the team just built. A facilitated wrap-up ties the experience back to how your team works.

Planning checklist

Charity bike build planning checklist
DecisionWhat to settleRule of thumb
HeadcountTotal participants and number of teamsTeams of five typically build one bike each, so divide headcount by five to estimate bikes
RoomAn indoor space with theater seating and room for build tablesHotel ballrooms work; confirm the layout with your provider before you sign the venue contract
Length60, 90, 120 or 180 minutesAbout two hours is typical. Choose 60 minutes for pure assembly, and longer when you want a framed opener and a debrief
RecipientWho receives the bikes, and whether the children attendAsk for a named, vetted local organization and a live handoff on the day
BudgetPer-person price and what it includes$100 to $175 per person, with the donated bikes and the children's visit included. Ask for the quote itemized
CalendarDate, and how it fits the agendaBook early. Sales kickoffs cluster in January and February, and those dates go first

Where the bikes go

Every bike goes to a child in the community where you hold the event, and each child receives a helmet, a lock and a backpack along with the bike. Boys & Girls Clubs are Legendary Team Building's number one recipient partner, and during school hours the programs also work with Title I elementary schools. A recipient who confirmed the need and attends the event is the strongest sign that a build will be more than a task.

Choosing a provider

Ask every company for the same things: an itemized quote, the named recipient, the number of bikes in writing, and proof of impact afterward. Our questions-to-ask list and provider scorecard covers each one. If you are comparing formats rather than companies, start with the decision guide, and see what corporate team building costs for the wider budget picture.

When a bike build is not the right choice

If you only want a low-stakes social, a lighter activity costs less. If you need multi-quarter organizational change, start with an OD or leadership firm and use a build as the event that kicks it off. For a general session of hundreds or thousands, a bike build scales well; see conference team building and charity team building for the full range of give-back formats, and how to measure the results.

Frequently asked questions

What is a corporate charity bike build? +

A corporate charity bike build is a team building activity in which employees assemble real, road-ready bikes that are donated to children in need. Legendary Team Building's version, Building a Dream, ends with the children arriving to receive the bikes, with a helmet, lock and backpack for each child.

How much does a corporate charity bike build cost? +

Building a Dream typically costs $100 to $175 per person, with the donated bikes and the children's visit included. The price moves with group size, length and location, so ask any provider for an itemized quote that shows facilitation, materials, the donation and setup separately.

How long does a charity bike build take? +

About two hours is typical. Building a Dream runs from 60 to 180 minutes. A 60-minute session is mostly hands-on assembly; longer sessions add an opening that connects the build to your message and a facilitated debrief.

How many people can take part in a charity bike build? +

Building a Dream works for groups of 5 to 5,000, including conference general sessions. Teams of five typically build one bike each, so a group of 100 builds about 20 bikes and a group of 5,000 builds about 1,000.

Where do the bikes go after the event? +

Every bike is donated to a child in the host community, often at the event itself. Boys & Girls Clubs are Legendary Team Building's number one recipient partner, and during school hours the programs also work with Title I elementary schools.

Do employees need any technical skill to build a bike? +

No. Each team gets a clear kit, no experience is needed, and the event crew safety-checks every finished bike.

When should we book a charity bike build? +

Book as early as you can. Sales kickoffs cluster in January and February, and those dates go first.
